rom.design: Qwen3-8B ROM, option C (2 packages, 4 dies, TP-4, G = 6,144 pruned, W12 wires, 8K)

exchange.source: MEASURED on the V4.1 TP-4 group (W15 v41p17_r0d1024 fit: 2 packages x 2 dies, direct T1 board links), transferred to the Qwen payload and clock

product.superseded: 2-die package, W5 wires: 9,851 tok/s (does not fit at 75 Mbit/mm2)

rom.capacity_basis: each die's 4 HBM3E stacks x 22.5 GB x 0.90 over its 2 of 8 KV heads of one 8K user (604.0 MB a user)

energy.basis: the uarch constants (technology.json), 2 ops per MAC, all 4 dies; ROM area at the storage-only density

rom.note: m = 1: batching reuses no weight word, so the lanes, the stream unit and the KV stream each cap the aggregate; the KV stream (each user's 604 MB of 8K FP8 KV per token over 16 stacks) binds first

dflash.note: best block per batch (tau per block from results/speculative/dflash_block_acceptance.json); users x block positions share the 16 MMA columns, a pass per 16

hbm.capacity_basis: 8 stacks x 22.5 GB x 0.90 less the INT8 weights, over 604 MB per user

energy.basis: SM MACs (2 ops, BF16 lane) + the whole HBM path per byte (technology.json hbm_j_per_byte, die + stack) + SMEM staging write and read + stream elements; static: SM logic, SMEM + L2 SRAM, 4 HBM PHY + UCIe as logic, HBM interface idle

FAB.wafer_basis: S. Khan, A. Mann, 'AI Chips: What They Are and Why They Matter', CSET 2020: TSMC 5 nm wafer ~ $16,988 (estimate; cited)
FAB.d0_basis: TSMC 2020 Technology Symposium: N5 D0 ~0.10-0.11 /cm2 at the HVM ramp, < 0.1 after (reported by AnandTech / Tom's Hardware); cited
FAB.alpha_basis: ASSUMED negative-binomial clustering (Stapper); no harvesting or redundancy on any design
FAB.package_basis: Raymond James via Silicon Analysts: CoWoS-S ~$750 (H100: 814 mm2 + 5-6 HBM stacks, ~2,500 mm2 interposer), CoWoS-L ~$1,100 (B200); cited analyst estimates
FAB.test_basis: Raymond James (H100 test and assembly ~$920 a package); cited analyst estimate
FAB.hbm_basis: economics section (ASSUMED $360 a 24 GB stack; RJ's H100 80 GB HBM3 at ~$1,350 is ~$17/GB)
FAB.mask_basis: via-programmable ROM (adopted): base sets x $15M + 1 x $0.5M (low) .. 2 x $1M (high) coding masks per ROM die; every HBM comparator die design also pays one full set; / 1,000 production units

COST.package_basis: iso-package: every two-reticle + 8-HBM3E CoWoS-L-class package (the ROM packages, the HBM comparator packages and a B200 alike) at the repository's B200 device price (configs/hardware/architectures.json NVIDIA-B200-x1 cost_per_device, graded assumed)
COST.silicon_basis: technology_inputs.json wafer_cost_per_device (assumed) over the 46,225 mm2 wafer-scale device
